questions.prompt: In the saliva test, why did the starch tube with water stay blue-black?
options: It was the control: without saliva, the starch wasn't digested
questions.explain: The control shows it was the saliva that digested starch.

questions.prompt: Why is the inner wall of the small intestine covered with millions of finger-like villi?
options: To give a huge surface area for absorbing nutrients
questions.explain: More surface area means faster absorption into the blood.

questions.prompt: How does food move down the oesophagus?
options: By waves of muscle contraction called peristalsis

questions.prompt: The small intestine is about 6.5 m long and the whole digestive tract is about 8.75 m. What percentage of the tract is small intestine (to the nearest whole number)?
Plan an experiment to show that saliva digests starch.
questions.modelAnswer: Put equal volumes of starch solution in two test tubes. Add 2 mL of diluted saliva to tube A and 2 mL of water to tube B (the control). Keep both in a warm water bath at about 37 °C. Every 2 minutes, take a drop from each tube and test it with iodine on a white tile. Record the time when tube A no longer turns blue-black. Tube B should stay blue-black, showing saliva, not time or warmth, digested the starch.
